title: Saving and Investing: Simple and Compound Interest
seo_title: Grade 8 Simple and Compound Interest and Saving Worksheets (TEKS 8.12C, 8.12D, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.12C explain how small amounts of money invested regularly, including money saved for college and retirement, grow over time; 8.12D calculate and compare simple interest and compound interest earnings
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.12C and 8.12D: simple and compound interest, regular deposits and saving for college and retirement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Compound interest earns interest on interest.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Simple interest is earned only on the original amount: I = Prt.
  • Compound interest is earned on the balance, including past interest: multiply by (1 + r) each year.
  • Saving small amounts regularly adds up, and interest makes it grow even more.
  • Starting early gives money more time to grow.

Examples

Example

$1,000 at 10% for 2 years

Simple: $200

Compound: 1,000 × 1.1² = $1,210

Answer: compound earns $10 more

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Treating compound like simple interestEach year's interest is added before the next year.
Forgetting the depositsAdd every deposit and the interest each one earns.
Adding the rate instead of multiplyingMultiply by 1.05, do not add 5.
